blockers.detail: D6 forbids inferring or defaulting migrated structural confidence, including using not_applicable merely to satisfy validation. Confidence remains absent until evidence-backed enrichment or a separately accepted structural-confidence schema policy supplies a non-fabricating representation.
D3 preserves Autism list-valued uncertainty reduction conditions as legacy-unmapped; the current v0.2 Claim schema still requires embedded Uncertainty records.

D8 accepts the Botha correction, D11 preserves separate Singer edition identities, D12 accepts 2017-09-05 for the future non-authoritative revised-print Evidence identity, D13 accepts three edition-specific compatible bindings, and D14 accepts the remaining 2016 Kindle -> Claim 2 compatible binding on the strengthened follow-up evidence. The follow-up provenance distinction remains explicit: Singer's July 2016 announcement identifies the Kindle edition and hosts the publisher's framing description, while Dwyer 2022 cites Singer 2016 by Kindle location and characterises Singer as taking a middle ground; Dwyer's later intervention framework remains Dwyer's. The 2016 day-level publication date remains deliberately unaccepted because 2016-07-03 is still supported only by secondary catalogue data. No Claim support is copied automatically between editions.
Neurodiversity has list-valued legacy uncertainty reduction conditions and no accepted v0.2 mapping decision.
Neurodiversity also has broader_than -> adhd. D5 does not authorise expanding the paired candidate to ADHD, so the edge remains separately unresolved.
